summary: Authenticate private Core-to-OCPI callbacks with per-command capabilities and exact cached owner context; map Core terminal failures to standard OCPI results, arbitrate terminal choices with cache claims, fail closed on unconfigured administrative access, and bound callback transports with sanitized logs.
migration: Private callback callers must preserve the capability query parameter generated by the upgraded OCPI executor; UUID-only callbacks are rejected. Drain pending commands before replacing OCPI instances or cache topology; legacy pending callbacks have no capability context. All OCPI workers for a command must use the same shared cache; memory cache is process-local. Optional administrative access requires complete OCPI_ADMIN_JWKS_URI, OCPI_ADMIN_ISSUER, OCPI_ADMIN_AUDIENCE and comma-separated OCPI_ADMIN_ALLOWED_SUBJECTS; trusted issuer subjects must be reserved from tenant self-service credentials. Without configuration administrative endpoints return 503. Existing configured oidc objects need explicit audience and allowedSubjects. Core callback transport keeps its standard wire body and optional OIDC, with 5-second attempt and 15-second overall limits; OCPI partner result delivery has a 5-second deadline and 64-KiB response bound and does not follow redirects. Public OCPI Token authentication and standard command/result bodies are unchanged. Claims and delivery are not transactional or durable: retain existing pre-delivery resolution behavior, no automatic retry after ambiguous partner delivery, and no exactly-once guarantee. Coordinate rollout/rollback with drained commands and matching OCPI source/config/cache consumers; do not restore public administrative access. No database migration or deployment is performed by this change.
